Net takeaway adjusted with FSR context: The FOMC statement’s tone is clearly negative—highlighting steep output declines, surging job losses, muted inflation, impaired credit, and “considerable risks” to the outlook. The Federal Reserve’s zero lower bound stance, open-ended Treasury and agency MBS/CMBS purchases, and robust repo/ON RRP operations provide meaningful offsets.

The Financial Stability Report reinforces both sides of this balance. It documents acute March 2020 market stress—Treasury and short-term funding market dysfunction, outflows from money market funds, and elevated business leverage—along with rising credit risk and high uncertainty. At the same time, it shows that policy backstops rapidly restored market functioning, narrowed spreads, and reopened issuance; banks entered the shock with strong capital and liquidity; and household leverage was moderate relative to past cycles. These factors reduce tail risks even as vulnerabilities (notably elevated corporate debt and fragile short-term funding structures) keep the near-term risk backdrop adverse.

Net effect: still negative, but less so than a reading focused only on downside risks, given improved market functioning and system resilience highlighted in the FSR.
